notes: Landscape, straight-on through a shop window on Charing Cross Road in daylight; the glass carries reflections of the street and the photographer across every shelf, and the gilt lettering on the leather spines is small and low-contrast. English, one Latin title. Antiquarian sets are labelled once per work: Blackstone's Commentaries (4 vols), Doré Gallery (2 vols), Wealth of Nations (3 vols, spine 'Smith's Wealth of Nations'), the Jane Austen set is labelled by volume (Vol I-V carry the novel titles). Pride and Prejudice is also a face-out Hugh Thomson edition. Partial: London Labour and the London Poor (spine reads 'Mayhew's London Labour' Vol I-III), Spain (blue decorative spine, only 'SPA' clear), London: A Pilgrimage (Doré, 'LOND' hidden by the neighbour), The Botanic Garden (spine 'Darwin's Botanic Garden'), The Works of Edmund Burke ('Burke's Works' Vol I-II), History of England ('Macaulay's England' Vol I-V), History of Latin Christianity (purple spine, part legible), The Science and Art of Surgery ('Erichsen's Surgery' Vol I), Vegetable Mould and Earth-Worms and A Naturalist's Voyage Round the World (Darwin, dark spines with a few words legible), Wood's Natural History (Vol I-III, series title only). Left out: the prints and plates in sleeves on the top shelf (bird and butterfly plates, a Leonardo title page which is the Treatise on Painting), the green gilt set far left (no readable title), the three tan spines centre-right of the top shelf, the fawn set and the row of tan volumes centre of the middle shelf, most of the right half of the middle shelf and the right half of the bottom shelf (gilt labels too small through the glass), the plain paper-covered rows above, and the book with 'Cooper's Surgical Essays' in faint type. Drafted by claude-sonnet-5 (extraction 90), verified by an agent.
